title: Structures
summary: Build three small craft-stick frames, no diagonals, one diagonal and full triangles, and load each to failure to find out which shape actually holds weight.
materials: hot glue gun and glue sticks, adult supervised
small paper cups and washers or pennies

figure.alt: Three same-size rectangular frames, fifteen by ten centimetres, are sketched side by side: one with no bracing inside, one with a single diagonal stick corner to corner, and one filled with a zigzag of sticks making triangles throughout.

steps.title: Ask, imagine, plan
steps.body:
The design loop, same as always: ask, imagine, plan, build, test, fix.

Ask: why do bridges and cranes look like they are made of triangles? A frame holding weight needs a shape that will not lean over under load.

Imagine: three small frames, all the same footprint, say a 15 by 10 centimetre rectangle. One with no bracing at all, one with a single diagonal stick across it, and one built entirely from triangles.

Plan: sketch all three on graph paper first, same outer size on every one, so the only real difference between them is how the sticks inside are arranged. An adult joins the safety brief before any hot glue is used today. The glue gun stays in a hand or its stand, never on the table, and it is hot enough to burn well after it looks cool.

figure.alt: A rectangle pushed at one corner leans into a slanted shape, shown as a dashed outline, because its corners are free to swing. A triangle pushed the same way does not lean at all, since none of its three sides can change length.

frames.caption: push the triangle the same way
it will not lean at all

steps.title: The triangle locks the shape
steps.body:
Pin four sticks loosely at their corners into a rectangle and push one corner sideways. It leans into a slanted shape without any stick changing length, because a rectangle's corners are free to swing.

Now pin three sticks into a triangle and push however hard feels safe. It will not lean. To change a triangle's shape, one of its three sides would have to get longer or shorter, and a rigid stick simply cannot do that. The triangle is the only shape whose side lengths alone lock every corner in place.

Add a single diagonal stick across a rectangle and it stops leaning too, because the diagonal and two of the rectangle's sides now form a triangle that cannot change shape. That is the whole trick behind trusses, bridges and roof frames. Fill a wobbly shape with triangles and the wobble has nowhere left to go, without needing much more material at all.

figure.alt: A satellite orbits high above Earth, moving fast sideways while constantly falling toward the planet. The ground curves away beneath it just as fast, so it circles forever instead of hitting the surface.

frames.caption: and it keeps falling toward Earth
but the curve carries it around

steps.title: Why a satellite never falls
steps.body:
A satellite is not held up by anything. It falls the whole time, the same way a thrown ball falls. It never hits the ground because the ground curves away beneath it just as fast.

GPS satellites orbit about 20,200 kilometres up, moving near 3.9 kilometres a second, circling the Earth once every 12 hours. Fly slower than the speed that matches your altitude and you spiral down. Fly faster and you climb to a higher, slower orbit instead.

A satellite closer to Earth needs more speed to keep falling around it rather than into it. The International Space Station, only about 400 kilometres up, travels near 7.7 kilometres a second, circling the planet every 90 minutes.

Your robot avoids a hand once it senses one. A satellite avoids the ground by moving exactly fast enough to keep missing it, forever.

figure.alt: A test frame stands on its edge with a paper cup hanging by a string from the middle of its top edge. Washers or pennies are added to the cup one at a time until the frame collapses or a glue joint gives way.

steps.title: Build three frames, load each to failure
steps.body:
With an adult present for all of today's hot glue work, build the no-diagonal frame first: four sticks glued into a rectangle, nothing crossing the middle. Build the one-diagonal frame next, the same rectangle with one stick glued corner to corner. Build the full-triangle frame last, filling the same outer rectangle with a zigzag of sticks so every enclosed shape is a triangle.

Build two copies of each design, six frames in total, so a weak glue joint on one copy does not get mistaken for a weak design.

Test each frame the same way: stand it on its edge and hang a paper cup from the middle of its top edge. Add washers or pennies one at a time until it visibly collapses or a joint gives way. Count the grams it held right before that happened, then move to the next frame.
checklist: All three designs share the same outer footprint, checked with the ruler
Two copies of each design were built and tested
Weight was added the same way, one piece at a time, on every frame
The no-diagonal frame failed at a clearly lower weight than the fully triangled one

steps.title: Design versus load held
steps.body:
The outer footprint, the sticks and glue, and how weight was added stay the same across every frame. Only the bracing inside changes, and each frame is loaded to failure only once since the test breaks it.

Six rows, two per design. For each row, write the design and the weight in grams it held right before it collapsed or a joint gave way.
steps.question: Which design held the most weight, and about how many times more than the no-diagonal frame?

steps.title: Bug diary
steps.body:
One line for each thing that did not work the first time and what you tried. Classics this week: a glue joint that lets go before the sticks do, testing the glue more than the shape.

Also watch for a frame that leans out of its footprint while drying, changing the outer size. And a paper cup that tips before the sticks fail stops the test early and needs a steadier hang point.

steps.title: Show it
steps.prompt: Photo of all three designs side by side before testing, and a photo of the fully triangled frame holding its heaviest load right before it failed
